precepts.text: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. That is the anointing of the most Holy: Christ.
precepts.point: So Christ's seventy times seven is the 490: the prophecy completed, the perfection of mercy delivered exactly on schedule, because we could not sacrifice in our captivities and needed him.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ told Peter to forgive seventy times seven, and Christ never put numbers out just to put them there. Seven represents completion, but what is seventy times seven? Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. That is 490 years, from Persia to Christ, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

Who is the most Holy that is anointed? Hebrews 1:9 explains it: “Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” That is talking about Christ. Where Daniel says “to anoint the most Holy”, that is Christ.

So the seventy weeks run “unto the Messiah the Prince”, which is Jesus Christ, and the reconciliation for iniquity and the end of sins come through him. The prophecy was 490 years, completing that perfection through Christ, because we needed that mercy. We couldn't sacrifice when we were enslaved under Babylon and Persia; we were always in captivity, going from one captivity to the next, so we needed Christ.

The apostles said it: “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel”. That is why he told Peter to forgive his brother seventy times seven: because he forgave us seventy times seven. He is that complete perfection. But don't take him for granted.

precepts.text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation? Who is going to be heir of salvation? Us, if we keep the commandments. The angels work on our behalf.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
The psalm calls the angels “ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” They minister unto the Most High, but they minister unto us as well: “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?”

Who is going to be heir of salvation? Us, if we keep the commandments. So the angels work on our behalf. They are ministering spirits, sent forth by God for his people.

So the angels that come before the Lord in Job 1 are not rebels running loose. They are sent forth at his word, whether to try a man like Job or to minister for the heirs of salvation.

precepts.text: Who maketh his angels spirits and his ministers a flame of fire: the spirits created for vengeance.
precepts.point: I will bring plagues upon the world, the sword, famine, death and destruction, for wickedness hath exceedingly polluted the whole earth; I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickedness. It starts with his spirit on us teaching, and then he comes back and deals with them.
precepts.why:
Sirach said there be spirits “created for vengeance.” Who are those spirits? Hebrews tells it: “And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.” The Lord makes his angels spirits. So the spirits created for vengeance are the angels.

That is how the Lord keeps his word in 2 Esdras 15, “I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” He does it through his angels, his ministers, a flame of fire, instigating these things in ways we cannot see.

And he says, “I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickedness.” God is not going to be quiet any more over all the evil being done upon this earth. It starts with him putting his spirit on us and we are teaching, speaking in the ears of his people the words of prophecy, and then he comes back and deals with them the same way.

precepts.text: Being but one she can do all things, and in all ages entering into holy souls she maketh them friends of God and prophets.
precepts.point: When he had by himself purged our sins he sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high; he is not standing in a corner on punishment while his Father has a throne.

precepts.text: God hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son; the last days began at Christ.
precepts.point: A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; as Hosea says, after two days He will revive us, and in the third day He will raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.” The latter days are the last days, and the last days began when Christ came on the earth, was crucified, and resurrected.

“God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.” In these last days He has spoken by His Son; the last days began at Christ.

So what Balaam advertised of the latter days is what Israel shall do to the nations from the time of Christ onward.

precepts.text: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake unto the fathers by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son; Christ's coming began the last days, and the Most High has always dealt through his prophets.
precepts.point: For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.
precepts.why:
“God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son”. The Most High has always dealt through his prophets, and Christ's coming began the last days.

That tells you when “the latter days” are: they began when Christ came. “When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice”. This is that time, and the turning begins with the spirit of fear, to get right with the Most High, seeking him with all thy heart and with all thy soul.

precepts.text: The angels are spirits and ministers made of the flame of fire that sits under the throne of heaven; they go and come as they please, change forms, vanish into thin air, and one of them can slay an hundred fourscore and five thousand men in a single night.
precepts.point: The angel greets him: the Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour. The Most High already saw the warrior in the man hiding wheat.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
An angel of the Lord “sat under an oak which was in Ophrah” and then “appeared unto” Gideon. What is an angel? “Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.”

The angels are spirits and ministers made of the flame of fire that sits under the throne of heaven. They go and come as they please, change forms, and vanish into thin air, and one of them can slay an hundred fourscore and five thousand men in a single night. That is the kind of being that sat down under the oak while Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, hiding his own harvest from the Midianites, and greeted him, “The Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.”

precepts.text: To the Son He says thy throne is forever and ever, a scepter of righteousness is the scepter of thy kingdom.
precepts.point: That rulership belongs to Christ from the tribe of Judah, and if we keep the commandments we will be heirs with Him in the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 45: Thy Throne, O God, Is Forever

precepts.why:
Hebrews shows exactly who Psalm 45:6 is spoken to. Of the Son the Father said, “Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee”, and “when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.” “And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire. But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.”

So the throne that is for ever and ever, and the right sceptre, belong to the Son, Christ from the tribe of Judah. The sceptre of righteousness is the right sceptre, and if we keep the commandments we will be heirs with him in that kingdom.

precepts.point: When it says 'according to the will of God and our Father,' God refers to Christ (who is called God in Hebrews 1:8) and Father refers to the Most High.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
“according to the will of God and our Father”: here God refers to Christ and Father refers to the Most High. Christ is called God in Hebrews: “But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.”

The Father speaks to the Son and calls him God. So when Paul writes of the will of God and our Father, it is the will of Christ and of the Most High.
